source_caption:
Loving Vincent (2017) is a truly one-of-a-kind achievement in animation history. The film became the world’s first fully painted animated feature, with every single frame created as an individual oil painting on canvas. More than 65,000 hand-painted frames were produced by a team of over 100 artists, all working in a style inspired by Vincent van Gogh’s iconic brushwork and artistic techniques.

What makes the film so extraordinary is that it doesn’t simply tell a story about Van Gogh—it feels as though his paintings have come to life. Every frame is filled with the colors, textures, and movement that made his artwork so distinctive, creating an experience unlike anything else in cinema.

Beyond its groundbreaking visuals, Loving Vincent explores the final days of Van Gogh’s life through a mystery-driven narrative, examining the people who knew him and the legacy he left behind. The result is both a stunning artistic achievement and a heartfelt tribute to one of history’s most influential painters.

More than a film, Loving Vincent is a moving canvas in motion—a celebration of art, creativity, and the enduring impact of Vincent van Gogh’s vision.

source_details.synopsis: Loving Vincent is a 2017 experimental adult animated historical drama film directed by Dorota Kobiela and Hugh Welchman, and written by Kobiela, Welchman, and Jacek Dehnel. It is based on the life of the painter Vincent van Gogh, in particular the circumstances of his death. It is the first fully painted animated feature film. The film is a co-production between Poland and the United Kingdom, funded by the Polish Film Institute, and partially through a Kickstarter campaign. The film stars Robert Gulaczyk, Douglas Booth, Jerome Flynn, Saoirse Ronan, Helen McCrory, Chris O'Dowd, John Sessions, Eleanor Tomlinson, and Aidan Turner.
